title: Daily Security Intelligence Briefing — September 26, 2026
summary: Active mass exploitation targeting Oracle PeopleSoft ERP software globally alongside emergency shutdown advisories for Kiteworks secure file transfer systems signal severe enterprise risk vectors (The Hacker News, BleepingComputer).

tier1.title: 1. Attackers Bypass WAFs to Exploit Oracle PeopleSoft Flaw and Deploy Web Shells

fields.label: Source & Article Link
fields.value: The Hacker News

fields.label: Technical Severity / Domain
fields.value: Enterprise Software / CVE-2026-35273 (Mass Exploitation)

fields.label: Why You Must Read This
fields.value: Google issued an urgent warning regarding renewed, widespread exploitation of an unauthenticated remote code execution vulnerability in Oracle PeopleSoft across multiple sectors globally. Threat actors linked to ShinyHunters are deploying Web Application Firewall bypass techniques to drop web shells on compromised servers. Because PeopleSoft houses mission-critical HR and financial data across thousands of organizations, unauthenticated remote access creates immense systemic risk.

fields.label: Recommended Immediate Action
fields.value: Audit web server logs for WAF bypass anomalies and web shell drops, and apply Oracle's official security patch for CVE-2026-35273 immediately.

tier1.title: 2. Kiteworks urges 6-hour server shutdown over potential zero-day attacks

fields.label: Source & Article Link
fields.value: BleepingComputer

fields.label: Technical Severity / Domain
fields.value: Secure File Transfer / Zero-Day Threat

fields.label: Why You Must Read This
fields.value: Secure file-transfer provider Kiteworks (formerly Accellion) instructed its enterprise customer base globally to shut down servers temporarily after federal intelligence authorities warned of an imminent attack campaign. The precautionary measure aims to shield organizations from potential zero-day exploitation targeting high-value sensitive files. Managed file transfer systems remain top-tier targets for ransomware syndicates and extortion actors seeking bulk data access.

fields.label: Recommended Immediate Action
fields.value: Follow Kiteworks emergency guidance to isolate or shut down managed file transfer appliances until software mitigations or patches are released.

tier2.title: 1. SharePoint RCE and MikroTik RouterOS Flaws Actively Exploited in the Wild

fields.label: Domain
fields.value: Enterprise Vulnerabilities

fields.label: Subject / Topic Summary
fields.value: CISA added Microsoft SharePoint Server (CVE-2026-65660) and MikroTik RouterOS flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. Microsoft confirmed reliable evidence of real-world attacks exploiting the SharePoint code injection vulnerability to achieve remote code execution.

fields.label: Key Technical & Strategic Takeaways
fields.value: CISA added CVE-2026-65660 (SharePoint RCE) to the KEV catalog following active in-the-wild exploitation.; On-premise SharePoint servers must be updated immediately to prevent unauthorized command execution.

fields.label: Essential Direct Quote
fields.value: As of 9/25/2026, Microsoft had reliable evidence of observed attacks against exploitation of this vulnerability.

fields.label: Source
fields.value: The Hacker News

tier2.title: 2. Zero-Click Vulnerabilities in Salesforce Agentforce Expose Wider AI Agent Risk

fields.label: Domain
fields.value: AI & Cloud Security

fields.label: Subject / Topic Summary
fields.value: Security researchers uncovered 'SalesBleed', a set of zero-click vulnerabilities in Salesforce Agentforce AI agents. The flaws allow remote prompt injection and unauthorized exfiltration of sensitive CRM database records via DNS queries without user interaction.

fields.label: Key Technical & Strategic Takeaways
fields.value: Zero-click prompt injection enables untrusted inputs to instruct AI agents to exfiltrate enterprise data.; Agentic workflows operating with elevated database privileges introduce unmonitored execution vectors into production CRMs.

fields.label: Essential Direct Quote
fields.value: The 'SalesBleed' set of weaknesses in Salesforce's Agentforce agents exposed CRM data to attackers via prompt injection and DNS exfiltration.

fields.label: Source
fields.value: Infosecurity Magazine

tier2.title: 3. ShinyHunters hacked Clop leak site using Grav CMS path traversal flaw

fields.label: Domain
fields.value: Threat Intelligence

fields.label: Subject / Topic Summary
fields.value: The Clop ransomware group was forced to relocate its data leak site to a new Tor location after threat actor group ShinyHunters hacked and defaced the server. The breach exploited an unauthenticated path traversal flaw in the Grav CMS software hosting the portal.

fields.label: Key Technical & Strategic Takeaways
fields.value: Ransomware infrastructure remains susceptible to exploitation through standard public CMS vulnerabilities.; Conflict between rival cybercrime groups continues to expose backend threat actor operational assets.

fields.label: Essential Direct Quote
fields.value: The Clop ransomware gang has moved its data leak site to a new Tor address after confirming its previous server was compromised and defaced...

fields.label: Source
fields.value: BleepingComputer

tier2.title: 4. PamStealer macOS Malware Adds Live C2 Payload Decryption and Multi-Layer Persistence

fields.label: Domain
fields.value: Endpoint Security

fields.label: Subject / Topic Summary
fields.value: Threat researchers identified an updated variant of PamStealer malware targeting macOS users. The new version utilizes JavaScript for Automation (JXA) droppers combined with server-side decryption keys, preventing static payload analysis until live C2 communication occurs.

fields.label: Key Technical & Strategic Takeaways
fields.value: PamStealer requires live C2 server key exchange to reconstruct its primary payload dynamically.; Attackers continue leveraging macOS JXA scripting features to bypass conventional endpoint detection controls.

fields.label: Essential Direct Quote
fields.value: Where earlier variants embedded their payload key material, the latest artifacts ensure that the main payload can only be recovered using a server-side decryption chain.

fields.label: Source
fields.value: The Hacker News

tier2.title: 5. Threat detection dashboards are masking security coverage gaps

fields.label: Domain
fields.value: Security Operations

fields.label: Subject / Topic Summary
fields.value: An analysis of nearly 15,000 active detection rules across SIEM, EDR, and cloud tools revealed that 47% fail to fire during simulated adversary testing. Security teams relying strictly on dashboard indicators face significant blind spots in active threat detection.

fields.label: Key Technical & Strategic Takeaways
fields.value: 47% of deployed detection rules fail to trigger when subjected to real-world attack techniques.; Organizations must complement metric dashboards with automated breach and attack simulation to validate detection posture.

fields.label: Essential Direct Quote
fields.value: A detection rule can show up as deployed on a coverage dashboard and still never fire when an attacker uses the technique it was built to catch.

fields.label: Source
fields.value: Help Net Security
